_comment: Single source of truth for the image → Meshy → GLB pipeline (godot/tools/meshy_pipeline.py) and the Hero Studio page (godot/tools/hero_uploader/index.html). kind: hero → assets/3d/characters/heroes/<file>; demon → assets/3d/characters/demons/<file>; prop → assets/3d/props/<file>. keys = CharLayer.char_key() values that should route to this model (CharLayer reads this file at start and routes every hero key to its file; the hand table PORTRAIT_3D_KEY_TO_GLB still wins where it has an entry). Entries flagged notes=SPARSE have a proposed look where canon says nothing — edit before spending credits. 2026-09-26: +36 heroes (the vol6 cast that had no entry: Eileen, BT, Anita, Coach K, the Centro night shift, the team) and LOOKS — an entry with base/look is another age or costume of the same person (Maya at 7, Miriam nine years on, Ben in pads and in the TE-1 jersey, Anita in scrubs, Coach K at home).

_schema.slug: unique id, [a-z0-9_]; also the folder under assets/concept/meshy/
_schema.name: display name in Hero Studio; substituted for {name} in the style preamble unless prompt_name is set
_schema.file: canonical GLB filename (must match CharLayer / HERO_GLB_PATHS)
_schema.keys: speaker keys (char_key()) that should resolve to this model
_schema.tag: one-line canon note shown in the UI
_schema.aspect: concept image aspect: 3:4 for figures, 1:1 for objects, 4:3/16:9 for vehicles
_schema.pose: a-pose | t-pose | null (Meshy pose_mode; null for props)
_schema.prompt: hand-written fallback description, used only when the text has no canon quotes (or appended when prompt_mode = append)
_schema.texture_prompt: optional Meshy texture guidance (<= 600 chars); defaults to prompt
_schema.notes: SPARSE = canon says little; the look is proposed — edit before spending credits
_schema.canon: list of {src, text}: VERBATIM sentences from the story text describing the look. When present these ARE the description sent to the image model; `prompt` is then only a fallback (or extra direction when prompt_mode is 'append'). Fill/refresh with godot/tools/meshy_canon.py.
_schema.prompt_mode: fallback (default: prompt used only when canon is empty) | append (prompt added after the canon quotes)
_schema.base: slug of the hero this entry is a LOOK of (another age or costume of the same person) — its own concept image and GLB; omitted on a hero's default look
_schema.look: {label, vols, scenes?, when}: what this look is and where the scenes stage it. CharLayer routes a base key to this look's GLB when the current scene's vol is in `vols` — narrowed to the listed scene ids when `scenes` is given (a costume is a scene, not a volume); the look's own keys always route to it
_schema.looks: on a base entry: the slugs of its looks, for the Hero Studio to group under it
_schema.apply: ART only: where the picture goes — a list of {locale, center [x,y,z] in BLENDER coordinates, size [w,h] in metres, facing (+x|-x|+y|-y|up = the side the viewer stands on), hide [name prefixes of the box stand-in to hide when the picture is installed], label}. scripts/vn/HeroArt.gd lays the picture there when the locale loads.
_schema.prompt_name: optional: the name sent to the image model in place of `name` (a real person the text fictionalises goes without the real name, so the generator draws the text's figure, not a likeness)
_schema.setting: optional: where this subject's story is set, for {setting} in the style preamble; default = the place its `vol`s share in defaults.setting_by_vol, else defaults.setting
_schema.role: scene2d only: bg (a background the story plays over) | cg (a held story moment) | plate (a chapter's illustrated title page, lettered with its title; style.plate)
_schema.scenes: scene2d only: the scene ids that show this picture
_schema.lettering: art / scene2d: the exact words the picture carries (a sign, a title plate, a zine page); lifts the no-text rule for those words only
_schema.subject: scene2d only: 'places' = the picture shows the place and its objects with no people in it (style.subject_places) — the plates of vol 7, whose people never matched the cast
_schema.refs: optional: roster slugs (props, art) whose chosen front image is sent as a reference image with this entry's front (three at most), so a plate's objects match their own concept art

style.hero: Full-body concept render of {name}, a character from a literary visual novel set in {setting}. Standing in a relaxed A-pose (arms slightly away from the body, palms turned in), facing the camera straight on, feet flat and fully visible, whole body in frame with margin above the head and below the feet. Plain flat light-grey seamless studio background, even soft frontal lighting, no cast shadow on the background, nothing on the floor, one subject only. Grounded semi-realistic painterly style, natural proportions, clean readable silhouette, clothing colours clearly separated from skin and hair.
style.demon: Full-body concept render of {name}, an uncanny figure from a literary visual novel about thin places in {setting}. Standing in a relaxed A-pose (arms slightly away from the body), facing the camera straight on, feet visible, whole body in frame with margin. Plain flat light-grey seamless studio background, even soft frontal lighting, no cast shadow on the background, one subject only. Semi-realistic painterly style with a bold, exaggerated silhouette that reads at a distance (the in-game shader smears fine detail into digital static); muted palette with one sickly accent colour; almost human, wrong in one or two specific ways.
style.prop: Single-object concept render of {name}, a story-critical prop from a literary visual novel. The object alone, centered, three-quarter view from slightly above, whole object in frame with margin, on a plain flat light-grey seamless background with nothing under it, even soft studio lighting, no cast shadow on the background, no hands, no people, no other objects. Semi-realistic painterly style with a clear material read (worn wood, tarnished brass, creased paper, scuffed plastic).
style.suffix: No text, no captions, no labels, no watermark, no border.
style.view_side: Same subject, identical design, colours, clothing and details as the reference image, now seen from the left side in strict profile (90 degrees), same pose, same plain light-grey background, whole subject in frame.
style.view_back: Same subject, identical design, colours, clothing and details as the reference image, now seen directly from behind (180 degrees), same pose, same plain light-grey background, whole subject in frame.
style.hero_short: Full-body concept render of {name}: relaxed A-pose, facing camera, feet visible, whole body in frame, plain flat light-grey seamless background, even soft light, no cast shadow, one subject, semi-realistic painterly style, clean silhouette.
style.demon_short: Full-body concept render of {name}: uncanny figure, relaxed A-pose, facing camera, whole body in frame, plain flat light-grey seamless background, even soft light, one subject, bold exaggerated silhouette, muted palette with one sickly accent, almost human, wrong in one or two ways.
style.prop_short: Single-object concept render of {name}: the object alone, centered, three-quarter view from slightly above, whole object in frame, plain flat light-grey seamless background, even soft light, no hands, no other objects, clear material read.
style.art: A single flat image of {name}, an artwork that exists inside a literary visual novel. The image IS the artwork's surface, seen straight on and filling the whole frame edge to edge: no wall around it, no frame, no room, no perspective, no hands, no photographer, no shadows falling across it. Painterly realism, real materials (paint on brick, a photo print, ink on paper), true to the medium named in the description.
style.art_short: Flat straight-on image of {name}, the artwork alone filling the frame edge to edge, no wall, frame, room or perspective, true to its medium.
style.scene2d: A single full-screen still for a literary visual novel set in {setting}: {name}. Cinematic 16:9 composition that reads at a glance, painted realism at full modern resolution — natural light, real materials, depth and atmosphere, the colour of the hour the text names. Show what the description shows and nothing it does not. Never a retro or pixel-art look, never an old game's screen, no scanlines, no CRT curve, no film grain filter.
style.scene2d_short: Full-screen 16:9 still for a literary visual novel: {name}. Painted realism, natural light, real materials, depth; no retro or pixel-art look, no scanlines.
style.scene2d_bg: This is a BACKGROUND the story plays over: the place itself, an establishing view at eye height, no people in it unless the description puts them there, no one looking at the camera; keep the lower third calm and uncluttered (the dialogue box sits there).
style.scene2d_cg: This is a CG — one held moment of the story, framed like a film still on the subject the description names; figures appear only as the description gives them.
style.plate: The illustrated TITLE PAGE of one chapter of a literary visual novel set in {setting}: {name}. A single 16:9 picture, straight on, edge to edge: the chapter's lettering set large and clean in the middle third, in a typeface that suits the volume, and around and behind it a painted scene made from the imagery the description quotes, composed as one picture so the words stay readable. Painted realism at full modern resolution, real light and materials, the volume's palette; never a retro or pixel-art look, no scanlines, no CRT curve.
style.plate_short: Illustrated 16:9 chapter title page: {name}. The lettering large and clean in the middle; the chapter's imagery painted around it; modern painted realism.
style.subject_places: This picture shows the PLACE and its OBJECTS only: no people anywhere in it — no figures, faces, hands, bodies or silhouettes, near or far. The story's people are drawn elsewhere and must not appear here; let the things they left (a mug on a rail, a coat on a hook, a door standing open) say who was there.

entries.name: John Frank
entries.tag: 0 The Fool · also XIV Temperance / XIX The Sun

Wears the diner's plain white button shirt with sleeves rolled to the elbow, a black half-apron with a folded napkin tucked into it, dark trousers, scuffed black work shoes. Open, watchful face; a wanderer who hasn't left yet.

canon.text: He watched his own reflection in the glass — shadowed eyes, gaunt face, a young man at a counter waiting for his cue.

John Frank: grad student, mixed-media journalist (whatever that meant this week), late-night waiter at the nexus of Graustark, Texas/Louisiana, this riverboat-shaped restaurant wedged between reason and riot, between two states of being and two states of the union.
In John's coat pocket, against his ribs, the folded napkin from booth six pressed faintly through the lining.
John walks over from the diner with his notebook. He stands at the back of the crowd.
A middle-aged man in a Montreal apartment. Drinking adequate coffee. Observing the alley.
John Frank — 20-something, grad student, "mixed-media journalist," waiter.
twelve years at the counter
a small annotation on John's apron under the painted scene reads '12 yr'.

entries.name: Frasier Temple
entries.tag: I The Magician · Cathedral of Rust & Code
entries.prompt: Frasier Temple, young Black man in his late 20s, athletic build, locs twisted up and back off his forehead. A leather bomber jacket worn open, stained with solder flux and worse, showing a dark t-shirt with a cream gear logo (GEARING CORP) centered on the chest, dark jeans, dark sneakers. Focused, wry expression; a warehouse sysop who solders his own circuit boards.

canon.text: Leather bomber jacket stained with substances that might have been solder flux, might have been hot sauce, might have been transmission fluid, certainly were not, at this point, identifiable.
Frasier moved through it — lanky silhouette against the gloom. His bomber jacket draped over a t-shirt bearing the faded logo of some defunct tech collective the rest of the world had forgotten.
Young Black man (late 20s/early 30s, not "middle-aged creaky" — that quote from `_VOL6_WIKI.md` is about vol6-era Frasier; vol5 Frasier is young)
Locs / dreadlocks — twisted strands going up + back. NOT an afro.
Olive bomber jacket worn OPEN — two side panels visible, dark t-shirt visible in the chest gap
"GEARING CORP" tee — dark t-shirt with a cream/grey gear logo on the chest centerline (the printed band-tee / dev-shop vibe)
Pose canon: at his workbench in the Cathedral, holding a soldering iron in one hand, working on a circuit board with the other. Lean-forward posture, focused face.
He tapped the cover of his notebook. Diagrams adorned it that looked suspiciously like circuit boards woven into mandalas.
Hair a chaotic sculpture defying gravity and three of the laws of thermodynamics. Notebook tucked under his arm like a holy text or a bomb schematic, and possibly both.

entries.name: Elicia Temple
entries.tag: II The High Priestess · also XVI The Tower
entries.prompt: Elicia Temple (Duchane), documentary filmmaker in her early 30s, tall and composed. Dark hair pulled back, sharp intelligent eyes. Black turtleneck under a long charcoal coat, dark slim trousers, flat boots, a cassette recorder on a strap over one shoulder. The host of 'Whispers from the Liminal'; a veil of cassette tape ribbon hangs from her collar.
entries.texture_prompt: black wool turtleneck, charcoal wool coat, dark trousers, black leather boots, brown cassette tape ribbons

canon.text: The glow illuminated her face — sharp cheekbones and shadowed eyes. The polished mask she had built for the camera and then forgotten how to take off in private.

Her eyes — the pale, intelligent, evaluative eyes that had served her well in two industries and one unfortunate marriage — moved across the room in the practiced sweep of someone who could no longer enter a space without first checking the framing.
ELICIA — mid-thirties, dark hair tied back, no makeup — sits in a wooden chair, her hands folded in her lap.
wearing a denim jacket that had been repaired at the cuff and a scarf
He missed deciphering the coded warnings in Elicia Duchane's icy gaze across the D'Ambrosio's floor.
Even if her hands, lately, were starting to shake.
Her hair is down. Her face is bare.
Pale evaluative eyes. Two industries and one unfortunate marriage.
a scarf that had, she had told him, belonged to her mother

entries.name: Nicola Greer
entries.tag: III The Empress · hosts Aria
entries.prompt: Nicola Greer, 19, hostess on the D'Ambrosio riverboat. Slight, upright posture, chestnut hair in a neat low ponytail. Riverboat hostess uniform: fitted burgundy vest with brass buttons over a white blouse, black skirt to the knee, black flats, a small name badge. Bright, steady, a little too calm — she carries Aria.
entries.texture_prompt: burgundy velvet vest with brass buttons, white cotton blouse, black skirt, black flats, fair skin, chestnut hair

canon.text: She was chaos wrapped in a too-tight hostess uniform — untamed energy buzzing just beneath alabaster skin stretched taut over sharp cheekbones.
Nineteen, going on ancient. Nicola navigated the plush burgundy carpet — burgundy swamp, probably hiding generations of spilled secrets — with a practiced grace that was pure muscle memory.

Nicola Greer stood on the small landing, pale and exhausted, a duffel bag at her feet, her left hand pressed flat against her stomach in the gesture of a woman who had been making the gesture for some weeks without quite recognizing what the gesture was telling her.
Nicola Greer at the hostess stand, moving with that infuriating, oblivious grace, probably unaware she was carrying the next damn complication right there under her apron.

Back at the hostess stand, Nicola smoothed her uniform. The fabric suddenly felt alien, restrictive — a costume designed by a wardrobe department that had not consulted her and would not have listened if she'd asked.
He thought of Nicola Greer down on the floor, smiling the smile that did not reach her eyes.
The pocket of the apron Dante had embroidered with the boat's monogram in '23. Holds: pens, a folded reservation card, the small notebook you write checks in.
Nicola Greer. 19, going on ancient. Hostess at D'Ambrosio's riverboat. Friday night dinner. Pregnant — she felt the first kick this week.

entries.name: Dante D'Ambrosio
entries.tag: IV The Emperor · riverboat proprietor
entries.prompt: Dante D'Ambrosio, 60, proprietor of the riverboat diner. Stocky, barrel-chested, thick silver hair swept back, heavy brows, a broad Italian-American face. Dark three-piece suit with the jacket open, white shirt, no tie, a brass pocket-watch chain, polished black shoes. Stands like he owns the deck; a man about to be swallowed by the sinkhole.
entries.texture_prompt: dark navy wool suit, white shirt, brass watch chain, black leather shoes, olive skin, silver hair

canon.text: He stood up, smoothed his shirt — the white shirt with the red wine stain near the third button that he had not had the decency to change before service — and he walked out of the office, down the narrow stairs, into the heart of the boat that was both his kingdom and his cage.
A low groan of stressed timbers and rusting metal. Or maybe that was just his own bones settling deeper into the Louisiana muck side of the border. Sixty years old. Christ.

In front of the grill: THE CHAIRMAN. Late sixties. Crisp blue button-down rolled at the sleeves, khaki shorts, leather sandals. A canvas apron over the shirt — the apron is hand-printed across the chest in faded letters: **CHEZ HÉLÈNE · CHEF'S TABLE · 1979.**
Dante stood at the leaded window, bourbon in hand, and watched the man cross the gangway toward the parking lot.

The dining room received him the way a congregation receives a priest who has aged into a kind of permanent fixture: with the small reverent inattention of people who have stopped, decades ago, being surprised that he was still there.
Dante D'Ambrosio. 60. Proprietor of D'Ambrosio's riverboat. Sixty years of sweat and deals done in shadows thick as gumbo gravy.
His shoes were already wet. He could feel it, through the leather.
He was at the helm. He had been at the helm, on this particular morning, for sixty consecutive hours. He had not slept. He had not eaten.

entries.name: Quentin Paul
entries.tag: V The Hierophant · Table 17
entries.prompt: Quentin Paul, Graustark power figure in his 50s, immaculate. Silver-templed dark hair, clean-shaven, unreadable smile. Perfectly tailored charcoal suit, crisp white shirt, dark tie with a small gold pin, black oxfords shined to a mirror. Holds a pocket watch loosely in one hand. The man who brunches at Table 17.
entries.texture_prompt: charcoal wool suit, white shirt, dark silk tie, gold tie pin, black oxfords

canon.text: She saw the tension in his jaw. The slight tic near his eye.

Quentin Paul. Even from a distance, commanding attention. The suit still immaculate, despite the day's accumulated sweat and sin. He walked with that unwavering, purposeful gait — like a man marching toward either salvation or conquest, probably both.

He wasn't smiling. He wore a suit, even though it felt like the inside of a dog's mouth outside. His eyes swept over the small crowd leaving the service, pausing on folks here and there, like he was counting sins.
The war between spirit and ambition played out in the tense line of his shoulders, the tight clench of his jaw.
Paul adjusted his tie. Pulled out a phone. His voice carried faintly on the breeze — sharp, clipped, commanding.
Back when he was just another ambitious climber with sweat stains under his arms and hands that lingered a second too long when he handed back the check presenter.
He wasn't eating. He was delivering pronouncements between sips of black coffee.
Walks like he owns the damn sidewalk and maybe the sky too.
The way the cuff of his right sleeve was a millimeter shorter than the left, as if at some point that morning his hand had gripped it and twisted it down without his noticing.
Seminary school dropout, they said.

canon.text: Mackenzie at the bay, jacket damp, glasses fogging.
Mackenzie's coffee mug — the World's Okayest Weaver one — was in the sink, half-rinsed.

Mackenzie's weavin' somethin' bright on her loom — patterns nobody's seen before, curling patterns, organic, the kind you stared at for a while and then looked away from and then looked back and saw something new.
Mackenzie Roberts. Library-slash-daycare volunteer. Weaver. Older brother lost in the sinkhole three years ago. Pregnancy lost last year.
Mackenzie took the photograph from him. Held it in both hands, the way the boy had held the envelope.
Mackenzie had met them at the porch with a pitcher of iced tea.

canon.text: He tightened the wrench again. Knuckles white against the corroded metal. Pipe dope, plumber's tape, prayer — he'd tried it all.
Philip wiped his hands on a dishtowel that had been clean an hour ago and was no longer. He went to the door.
Philip Roberts the morning after the Polaroid. He has not, this Tuesday, slept much. He is on the lawn chair with the coffee from 6 AM still half-full.
Philip Roberts. Two beers in. The lawn chair.
Philip sits on the back step with his head in his hands and does not, today, come back into the kitchen.
Hear tell Philip's got the porch rebuilt. Sturdy this time.

canon.text: Antonio D'Ambrosio. 34. The younger son. The artista. Off in New Orleans chasing a fool dream with that punk Jimmy Daigle. Has two speeds: gone and about to be gone.
He ran a hand through his hair.
Antonio pinched the bridge of his nose. The phone hot against his ear.
you are in a borrowed white jacket on your father's floor.
You step into the locker room. The white jackets on the hooks. You take one off the second peg.
He was not, at thirty-four, ready for that to be true.
Antonio D'Ambrosio. The younger son. In New Orleans, in the cramped office above Ember & Ash. The wildcard. The artistic temperament.
The weight of his father's legacy, of Paul's expectations, pressing down.

entries.name: Douglas Forte
entries.tag: VIII Strength · ouroboros tattoo
entries.prompt: Douglas Forte, 40s, Joanna's lost lover. Rangy, weathered, close-cropped greying hair, a faded ouroboros tattoo (a snake eating its tail) visible on the inside of his right forearm. Wears an old dark confirmation suit a size too small, white shirt open at the collar, no tie, dusty dress shoes. Haunted, gentle.

canon.text: Scarred knuckles mapped with the ghosts of busted fences and kitchen brawls from back when Dante's word was law and Douglas's word, to the people who needed it, was Dante's.
The ouroboros on his forearm caught the neon and sent it back, dim and red, against the inside of his wrist.
The way her fingers — stained with ink or paint or charcoal, often all three at once — would trace the faded lines on his forearm where the snake tattoo ate its own tail.
The face looked back. Older than he remembered it being. Quieter. The kind of quiet that was not the same as peace.
Forte, with his quiet strength and his haunted eyes, didn't see the grift.
had driven up from New Orleans to sit in the back row in the suit his mother had bought him for his confirmation
Douglas Forte arrived on foot at the Roberts's house on Saturday morning, having walked for five days from New Orleans, his canvas duffle over his shoulder.
He had packed a bag — the same canvas duffle his father had carried back from Korea, which was now battered enough to look intentional
Calloused cartography of a life spent holding things together. Or maybe just holding on.

entries.name: Joanna LeMoine
entries.tag: IX The Hermit · also XVII The Star
entries.prompt: Joanna LeMoine, poet of the Graustark ruins, late 40s. Wiry, long grey-streaked dark hair loose under a battered wide-brim hat, weather-lined face, sharp eyes. Long oilskin coat over a wool sweater and corduroys, rubber boots, a lantern in one hand. A faded brown dog collar hangs from her belt (Rumpus).
entries.texture_prompt: dark green waxed oilskin coat, grey wool sweater, brown corduroy, black rubber boots, brass lantern

canon.text: He saw her sometimes, in the reflections distorted by cheap bar glass — a flash of unruly dark hair, eyes that held the wisdom of ruins.
She moved with a stillness that belied the tremor in her hands.
the obsidian ink staining her skin, the way it had been staining her skin in different patterns for the past three years, the way it had begun, in the past month, to outlast the soap she used.
She put it in the breast pocket of her jacket, the one that buttoned, the one she had stitched a small inner lining into precisely so that she could keep the things she was not yet ready to lose.
They had seen the cracks in her smile, the haunted hollows beneath her eyes.
Joanna sat down on a chunk of broken concrete, the moon-shard light falling across her shoulders, and allowed the animals their small comforts.

The Hermit, lantern held aloft — a scavenged flashlight, actually, flickering weakly, batteries Joanna had been meaning to replace for a week — led her small procession deeper into the beautiful terrifying labyrinth she now called home.
Saw her scrawling words on walls with charcoal fingers, surrounded by her court of stray dogs and one-eyed cats.
They had seen the girl who knew too much, felt too much, the one doomed to chronicle the fall because she was already halfway down.

entries.name: Erica Campbell
entries.tag: X Wheel of Fortune · also XI Justice
entries.prompt: Erica Campbell, Houston corporate lawyer, late 30s, Black woman with a precise close-cropped natural hairstyle and an expensive quiet confidence. Tailored navy pantsuit, cream silk blouse, low heels, a slim leather portfolio held at her side. Composed, sharp, kind under the armour.

canon.text: A woman — late twenties, ERICA CAMPBELL, although the deck does not yet permit naming her in the credits — enters. She wears a charcoal pencil skirt and a white blouse.
She took a breath. Smoothed her already immaculate suit jacket. The wheel was spinning. Time to place her bet.
the click as automatic now as her morning coffee, as the four small adjustments she made to her hair before any deposition, as the precise breath she took before any closing.
In Houston, high in her sterile tower, the Italian marble floor beneath Erica Campbell's expensive shoes did shudder
The phone, on the marble of her bedside table, had vibrated through the small brass dish she kept her earrings in
Precedents cross-referenced until her eyes burned, and the burn had begun to require its own eyedrop
Her face did the small careful nothing it did when she was being given information she needed to think about before she was visibly affected by it.

All-black outfit: boxy black linen shirt, wide black trousers, white sneakers, a sketchbook under one arm and a marker behind one ear. 'Corporate Idols' energy: polished, ironic.

canon.text: She adjusted her oversized, architecturally inspired glasses. This wasn't design; it was damage control.
Their relationship wasn't exactly passion; it was more like a peer-reviewed study in shared anxieties and meticulously curated vintage sweaters.
an older man in a charcoal suit, smoking carefully outside the no smoking sign, watched a young Houston designer cross the plaza without recognizing him
She saw Anna Logue in Houston polishing narratives that gleamed like lies, beginning, finally, to deconstruct one.

entries.name: Natalie David
entries.tag: XII The Hanged Man · also XVIII The Moon
entries.prompt: Natalie David, waitress and diviner in Simons, Louisiana, mid-40s. Dark curls tied up with a scarf, tired hooded eyes, silver rings on most fingers. Pale-yellow diner waitress dress with a white collar and a small stained apron, white sneakers, a tarot card tucked into the apron pocket. Half asleep, seeing everything.
entries.texture_prompt: pale yellow cotton waitress dress, white collar, white apron, white sneakers, silver rings, olive skin, dark curly hair

canon.text: Natalie has, in the last eight months, become someone whose reflection she does not immediately recognize · dark circles, hair unbrushed, the notebook-hunch in her shoulders.
She had set out, at twenty-two, to be a principal with a regional company in Atlanta. The setting-out had lasted six years.
The injury had taken something from her ankle and something from her left hip and a small bright permanent thing from her ability to trust her own balance.

canon.text: Since the age of fifteen, he was known as a hard-drinking, hard-hitting man. He was eventually killed at the age of thirty-three for allegedly raping a prominent mill owner's daughter.
He was often seen nursing a bottle, standing watch over her like a protective older brother — intimidating the rowdies who'd climb over the rail, wade into the pool, try and grab a feel.
A split tree had gashed David's arm — and while he was being tended to, he implored his father to go after the trapped girl.
He was a frequent and noisy drunk both on the job and off, and made few friends.
David grew up on the road. A brutal life for any child of that era — leaving his siblings dead and buried across the landscape of his youth.

A week after the disaster at Cliffside, while David holed up in rented lodgings on the physical mend, he wandered out onto the beach to watch the sunset and break the silence of his self-imposed exile.
David Jarvis was at once both reported killed in 1910 — and working as a fisherman later that year.
And to the select few that knew the young man, it was more a product of his psychological grief and torment than an actual real supernatural manifestation of the tragedy that lingered.

entries.prompt: A thirty-foot outdoor mural painted on an old brick alley wall in Smolvud, Oregon coast, seen flat-on in rainy gray-blue light. A deep indigo night-sky ground (RGB ~0.13/0.10/0.26) swirls into nebula bands of violet upper-left, teal lower-right and dusty rose across the top. Three clean-edged rectangles of the mural are simply gone, leaving almost-but-not-quite brick-colored patches (upper-left, upper-right, lower-right). Rain streaks down the wall. Flat, straight-on.

canon.text: The window over the kitchen sink looked out on the alley and on the wall of the building opposite, and on that wall was the Starfish Nebula mural Lena had painted across two months in the spring of 2050.
The patch now was past where the octopus had been, into the section where Lena had painted a triangular kite of starfish over what was meant to be a tide pool.

entries.tag: painted · salty_tome_interior · 6.05 x 1.56 m · 844 lines play here, 33 mention it
entries.prompt: The Starfish Nebula mural that Lena Vargas painted in spring 2050 on the brick back wall of the alley behind the Salty Tome bookshop in Smolvud, Oregon, seen flat and straight-on. Exterior paint on old red brick, mortar lines showing through. A deep indigo-violet night-sky ground (near black-purple) with a great five-armed starfish-shaped nebula sprawling across it: a dusty violet cloud arm upper left, a broad teal-green gas arm at the right, a warm rose-pink glow arm low on the left, cream and gold stars throughout, a bright star cluster upper right; along the lower edge painted sandstone arches like eroded sea-cave rock, and in the bottom-left quadrant a small playful octopus with seven and a half arms drifting among the stars. Confident, slightly naive brushwork softened by years of coastal rain: flaking at brick edges, drip runs. Very wide (about 3.9:1), evenly lit, nothing in front.

canon.text: The mural's bottom-left quadrant — the section where she had painted the small octopus with the seven and a half arms because she had been thinking, in spring of 2050, about how the octopus you painted should not be the octopus a person expected — was, this morning, half-eaten.

The patch had grown overnight — by what she could see at this distance, the patch had taken the right side of the sandstone arches sometime between when she had left the apartment yesterday morning and now.
